paper.title_en: Logic in Dynamical Stabilizer Quantum Error Correction Codes
paper.abstract_en:
Quantum error correction enables the protection of quantum information from noise arising from imperfect control and unwanted interactions with the environment. Manipulating logical information in quantum error-correcting codes remains challenging, as we can only directly access physical qubits, not the encoded logical qubits. In fact, we know it is not possible to get the full logical universal gate set by doing transversal physical operations. As a solution to this problem, many schemes for implementing encoded logical gates have been developed, including dynamical automorphism gates (DA). These logical protocols are realized by measurement sequences that transfer logical information between different codespaces. In parallel, there has been a growing interest in the intersection between quantum error correction and the ZX-calculus, a graphical representation of quantum processes. This direction has proved to be fruitful. For example, it has allowed the development of new dynamical codes. However, logic within such codes has not yet been tackled. In this thesis, we offer a formalism for dynamical automorphisms based on the ZX-calculus, implementing logical Clifford gates for stabilizer codes. We begin by defining the basics of quantum information, the stabilizer formalism and the ZX-calculus. Then, we build upon this formalism for gauge fixing via the ZX-calculus. Since gauge fixing may be implemented via measurement, our formalism allows us to protocols implementing dynamical automorphisms. In particular, we start by investigating a DA for a 3-qubit motivating code and its LC orbit. Then, we turn to an example of a logical CZ for the [[4, 2, 2]]code. Finally, we show an example of a distance-preserving dynamical automorphism for the [[7, 1, 3]] bare code implementing a phase gate, which was inaccessible using previous
techniques.
